title: JEE Main 2026 · 28 Jan · Shift 1 (recreated)

qs.stem: Let f be a polynomial function such that f(x<sup>2</sup> + 1) = x<sup>4</sup> + 5x<sup>2</sup> + 2, for all real x. Then ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>3</sup> f(x) dx is equal to
steps: Write x<sup>4</sup> + 5x<sup>2</sup> + 2 = (x<sup>2</sup>+1)<sup>2</sup> + 3(x<sup>2</sup>+1) − 2, so f(t) = t<sup>2</sup> + 3t − 2.
∫<sub>0</sub><sup>3</sup> (x<sup>2</sup> + 3x − 2) dx = [x<sup>3</sup>/3 + 3x<sup>2</sup>/2 − 2x] from 0 to 3.

qs.stem: Let S = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}. Let x be the number of 9-digit numbers formed using the digits of the set S such that only one digit is repeated and it is repeated exactly twice. Let y be the number of 9-digit numbers formed using the digits of the set S such that only two digits are repeated and each of these is repeated exactly twice. Then :
steps: For x: 8 distinct digits in all, chosen in <sup>9</sup>C<sub>8</sub> = 9 ways, pick the repeated one in 8 ways, arrange 9!/2: x = 9 × 8 × 9!/2 = 36 · 9!.
For y: 7 distinct digits in all, chosen in <sup>9</sup>C<sub>7</sub> = 36 ways, pick the two repeated ones in <sup>7</sup>C<sub>2</sub> = 21 ways, arrange 9!/(2!2!): y = 36 × 21 × 9!/4 = 189 · 9!.
So 21x = 756 · 9! = 4y.

qs.stem: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x dy/dx − sin 2y = x<sup>3</sup>(2 − x<sup>3</sup>) cos<sup>2</sup> y, x ≠ 0. If y(2) = 0, then tan (y(1)) is equal to :
steps: Divide by x cos<sup>2</sup>y: sec<sup>2</sup>y · dy/dx − (2/x) tan y = x<sup>2</sup>(2 − x<sup>3</sup>). Put z = tan y: dz/dx − (2/x) z = 2x<sup>2</sup> − x<sup>5</sup>.
Integrating factor 1/x<sup>2</sup>: z/x<sup>2</sup> = ∫(2 − x<sup>3</sup>) dx = 2x − x<sup>4</sup>/4 + C. Using y(2) = 0: 0 = 4 − 4 + C, so C = 0.
tan y = 2x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>6</sup>/4, so tan y(1) = 2 − 1/4 = 7/4.

qs.stem: Let A, B and C be three 2 × 2 matrices with real entries such that B = (I + A)<sup>−1</sup> and A + C = I. If BC = [[1, −5], [−1, 2]] and CB [[x<sub>1</sub>], [x<sub>2</sub>]] = [[12], [−6]], then x<sub>1</sub> + x<sub>2</sub> is :
steps: From B(I+A) = I = (I+A)B we get AB = BA, so B commutes with A and hence with C = I − A. Thus CB = BC = [[1, −5], [−1, 2]].
Solve x<sub>1</sub> − 5x<sub>2</sub> = 12 and −x<sub>1</sub> + 2x<sub>2</sub> = −6. Adding: −3x<sub>2</sub> = 6, so x<sub>2</sub> = −2 and x<sub>1</sub> = 2.
x<sub>1</sub> + x<sub>2</sub> = 0.

qs.stem: The value of ∑<sub>k=1</sub><sup>∞</sup> (−1)<sup>k+1</sup> ( k(k+1) / k! ) is :
steps: k(k+1)/k! = (k+1)/(k−1)! = 1/(k−2)! + 2/(k−1)! (the first term only for k ≥ 2).
∑(−1)<sup>k+1</sup>/(k−2)! (k ≥ 2) = −(1 − 1 + 1/2! − …) = −e<sup>−1</sup>, and 2∑(−1)<sup>k+1</sup>/(k−1)! (k ≥ 1) = 2e<sup>−1</sup>.
Total = −1/e + 2/e = 1/e (numerical partial sums also converge to 0.3679).

qs.stem: A bag contains 10 balls out of which k are red and (10 − k) are black, where 0 ≤ k ≤ 10. If three balls are drawn at random without replacement and all of them are found to be black, then the probability that the bag contains 1 red and 9 black balls is :
steps: Assuming each k is equally likely, P(3 black | k) is proportional to <sup>10−k</sup>C<sub>3</sub>.
Sum over k = 0..10 of <sup>10−k</sup>C<sub>3</sub> = <sup>3</sup>C<sub>3</sub> + … + <sup>10</sup>C<sub>3</sub> = <sup>11</sup>C<sub>4</sub> = 330.
k = 1 gives <sup>9</sup>C<sub>3</sub> = 84, so the probability is 84/330 = 14/55.

qs.stem: Let z be a complex number such that |z − 6| = 5 and |z + 2 − 6i| = 5. Then the value of z<sup>3</sup> + 3z<sup>2</sup> − 15z + 141 is equal to :
steps: The circles have centres (6, 0) and (−2, 6), both radius 5; the distance between centres is 10, so they touch externally at the midpoint, z = 2 + 3i.
z satisfies z<sup>2</sup> − 4z + 13 = 0. Dividing: z<sup>3</sup> + 3z<sup>2</sup> − 15z + 141 = (z<sup>2</sup> − 4z + 13)(z + 7) + 50.
Hence the value is 50 (direct check: z<sup>3</sup> = −46 + 9i, 3z<sup>2</sup> = −15 + 36i, −15z = −30 − 45i, sum with 141 gives 50).

qs.stem: If g(x) = 3x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 3, f(0) = −3 and 4g(f(x)) = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 32x + 72, then f(g(2)) is equal to :
steps: 4(3f<sup>2</sup> + 2f − 3) = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 32x + 72 gives 12f<sup>2</sup> + 8f − (3x<sup>2</sup> − 32x + 84) = 0. Its discriminant is 64 + 48(3x<sup>2</sup> − 32x + 84) = (12x − 64)<sup>2</sup>.
f = (−8 ± (12x − 64))/24. The condition f(0) = −3 selects the + sign, so f(x) = (x − 6)/2.

qs.stem: For three unit vectors a, b, c satisfying |a − b|2 + |b − c|2 + |c − a|2 = 9 and |2a + kb + kc| = 3, the positive value of k is :
steps: Each |u − v|2 = 2 − 2u·v for unit vectors, so the sum is 6 − 2S = 9, where S = a·b + b·c + c·a, giving S = −3/2.
Then |a+b+c|2 = 3 + 2S = 0, so b + c = −a.
|2a + k(b+c)| = |(2 − k)a| = |2 − k| = 3, so k = 5 (positive) or −1.

qs.stem: If tan(A − B)/tan A + sin<sup>2</sup>C / sin<sup>2</sup>A = 1, A, B, C ∈ (0, π/2), then :
steps: Let x = tan A, y = tan B, z = tan C. Then tan(A−B)/tan A = (x − y)/(x(1 + xy)) and sin<sup>2</sup>C/sin<sup>2</sup>A = z<sup>2</sup>(1 + x<sup>2</sup>)/(x<sup>2</sup>(1 + z<sup>2</sup>)).

Try z<sup>2</sup> = xy: the second term becomes y(1 + x<sup>2</sup>)/(x(1 + xy)), and the sum is (x − y + y + yx<sup>2</sup>)/(x(1 + xy)) = 1. The second term is strictly increasing in z<sup>2</sup>, so z<sup>2</sup> = xy is the only solution.
So tan<sup>2</sup>C = tan A tan B: tan A, tan C, tan B are in G.P.
opts: tan A, tan C, tan B are in A.P.
tan A, tan C, tan B are in G.P.
tan A, tan B, tan C are in G.P.
tan A, tan B, tan C are in A.P.

qs.stem: The common difference of the A.P.: a<sub>1</sub>, a<sub>2</sub>, …, a<sub>m</sub> is 13 more than the common difference of the A.P.: b<sub>1</sub>, b<sub>2</sub>, …, b<sub>n</sub>. If b<sub>31</sub> = −277, b<sub>43</sub> = −385 and a<sub>78</sub> = 327, then a<sub>1</sub> is equal to :
steps: Let the common difference of the b-progression be d. b<sub>43</sub> − b<sub>31</sub> = 12d = −108, so d = −9.
The a-progression has common difference d + 13 = 4.
a<sub>78</sub> = a<sub>1</sub> + 77 × 4 = 327, so a<sub>1</sub> = 327 − 308 = 19.

qs.stem: The area of the region R = {(x, y) : xy ≤ 8, 1 ≤ y ≤ x<sup>2</sup>, x ≥ 0} is :
steps: y ≥ 1 and y ≤ x<sup>2</sup> need x ≥ 1; the curves y = x<sup>2</sup> and y = 8/x meet at x = 2, and y = 8/x meets y = 1 at x = 8.
Area = ∫<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> (x<sup>2</sup> − 1) dx + ∫<sub>2</sub><sup>8</sup> (8/x − 1) dx = 4/3 + (8 ln 4 − 6).

qs.stem: Let ABC be an equilateral triangle with orthocenter at the origin and the side BC on the line x + 2√2 y = 4. If the co-ordinates of the vertex A are (α, β), then the greatest integer less than or equal to |α + √2 β| is :
steps: In an equilateral triangle the orthocenter is the centroid, so A is on the perpendicular from the origin to BC, at twice the distance on the opposite side of the foot D: A = −2D.
The foot of the perpendicular from the origin to x + 2√2 y = 4 is D = 4(1, 2√2)/9 = (4/9, 8√2/9).
A = (−8/9, −16√2/9), so |α + √2 β| = |−8/9 − 32/9| = 40/9 ≈ 4.44, whose integer part is 4.

qs.stem: If ∫ ( (1 − 5cos<sup>2</sup>x) / (sin<sup>5</sup>x cos<sup>2</sup>x) ) dx = f(x) + C, where C is the constant of integration, then f(π/6) − f(π/4) is equal to :
steps: Split the integrand as sec<sup>2</sup>x / sin<sup>5</sup>x − 5/sin<sup>5</sup>x. Guess f(x) = tan x / sin<sup>5</sup>x and differentiate: sec<sup>2</sup>x/sin<sup>5</sup>x − 5 tan x cos x / sin<sup>6</sup>x = sec<sup>2</sup>x/sin<sup>5</sup>x − 5/sin<sup>5</sup>x, which matches.
f(π/6) = (1/√3) · 32 = 32/√3, and f(π/4) = 1 · (√2)<sup>5</sup> = 4√2.
Difference = 32/√3 − 4√2 = (4/√3)(8 − √6).

qs.stem: If the distances of the point (1, 2, a) from the line (x − 1)/1 = y/2 = (z − 1)/1 along the lines L<sub>1</sub> : (x − 1)/3 = (y − 2)/4 = (z − a)/b and L<sub>2</sub> : (x − 1)/1 = (y − 2)/4 = (z − a)/c are equal, then a + b + c is equal to :
steps: Let A = (1, 2, a). L<sub>1</sub> meets the given line (direction (1, 2, 1) through (1, 0, 1)) at A + λ(3, 4, b). Matching x−1 = 3λ with y/2 = 1 + 2λ gives λ = 1, and then z − 1 = 3 gives a + b = 4 (point (4, 6, 4)).
L<sub>2</sub> meets it at A + μ(1, 4, c): μ = 1 + 2μ gives μ = −1, and z − 1 = μ gives a − c = 0, so c = a (point (0, −2, 0)).
Equal distances: 9 + 16 + b<sup>2</sup> = 1 + 16 + c<sup>2</sup>, i.e. c<sup>2</sup> − b<sup>2</sup> = 8 with c = a, b = 4 − a: 8a − 16 = 8, a = 3, b = 1, c = 3.

qs.stem: The value of lim<sub>x→0</sub> log<sub>e</sub>( sec(ex) · sec(e<sup>2</sup>x) · … · sec(e<sup>10</sup>x) ) / ( e<sup>2</sup> − e<sup>2cos x</sup> ) is equal to :
steps: Numerator = −∑<sub>k=1</sub><sup>10</sup> ln cos(e<sup>k</sup>x) ≈ ∑ (e<sup>k</sup>x)<sup>2</sup>/2 = (x<sup>2</sup>/2) ∑ e<sup>2k</sup> for small x.
Denominator = e<sup>2</sup>(1 − e<sup>2cos x − 2</sup>) ≈ e<sup>2</sup>(2 − 2cos x) ≈ e<sup>2</sup>x<sup>2</sup>.
Limit = (1/(2e<sup>2</sup>)) ∑<sub>k=1</sub><sup>10</sup> e<sup>2k</sup> = (1/(2e<sup>2</sup>)) · e<sup>2</sup>(e<sup>20</sup> − 1)/(e<sup>2</sup> − 1) = (e<sup>20</sup> − 1)/(2(e<sup>2</sup> − 1)).

qs.stem: The mean and variance of 10 observations are 9 and 34.2, respectively. If 8 of these observations are 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 13, 15, 21, then the mean deviation about the median of all the 10 observations is :
steps: The eight given values sum to 80, so the other two satisfy x + y = 90 − 80 = 10. Their squares: ∑x<sup>2</sup> = 10(34.2 + 81) = 1152, and the eight known squares add to 1094, so x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 58, giving xy = 21 and {x, y} = {3, 7}.
Absolute deviations: 6.5, 5.5, 5.5, 3.5, 1.5, 1.5, 2.5, 4.5, 6.5, 12.5, total 50, so the mean deviation = 50/10 = 5.

qs.stem: If α, β, where α < β, are the roots of the equation λx<sup>2</sup> − (λ + 3)x + 3 = 0 such that 1/α − 1/β = 1/3, then the sum of all possible values of λ is :
steps: 1/α − 1/β = (β − α)/(αβ) with β − α = √((λ+3)<sup>2</sup> − 12λ)/|λ| = |λ − 3|/|λ| and αβ = 3/λ. So the expression equals (λ/|λ|)|λ − 3|/3 = 1/3, which needs λ > 0 and |λ − 3| = 1.
λ = 2 or 4 (check: λ = 2 gives roots 1, 3/2; λ = 4 gives roots 3/4, 1; both satisfy the condition).

qs.stem: Let y = x be the equation of a chord of the circle C<sub>1</sub> (in the closed half-plane x ≥ 0) of diameter 10 passing through the origin. Let C<sub>2</sub> be another circle described on the given chord as its diameter. If the equation of the chord of the circle C<sub>2</sub>, which passes through the point (2, 3) and is farthest from the center of C<sub>2</sub>, is x + ay + b = 0, then a − b is equal to :
steps: C<sub>1</sub> has radius 5, lies in x ≥ 0 and passes through the origin, so it touches the y-axis there: centre (5, 0). The line y = x cuts it where 2x<sup>2</sup> − 10x = 0, i.e. at (0, 0) and (5, 5).

C<sub>2</sub> has diameter from (0, 0) to (5, 5): centre (5/2, 5/2). The point (2, 3) is inside it. The chord through (2, 3) farthest from the centre is perpendicular to the line joining the centre and (2, 3).
That radius has slope (3 − 5/2)/(2 − 5/2) = −1, so the chord has slope 1: y − 3 = x − 2, i.e. x − y + 1 = 0. Hence a = −1, b = 1 and a − b = −2.

qs.stem: Let S = {x<sup>3</sup> + ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c : a, b, c ∈ N and a, b, c ≤ 20} be a set of polynomials. Then the number of polynomials in S, which are divisible by x<sup>2</sup> + 2, is :
steps: Divide: x<sup>3</sup> + ax<sup>2</sup> + bx + c = (x<sup>2</sup> + 2)(x + a) + (b − 2)x + (c − 2a).
Divisibility needs b = 2 and c = 2a.
With a, c in 1..20, c = 2a ≤ 20 gives a = 1, ..., 10, so there are 10 polynomials.

qs.stem: In a G.P., if the product of the first three terms is 27 and the set of all possible values for the sum of its first three terms is R − (a, b), then a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> is equal to ________.
steps: Write the terms as 3/r, 3, 3r (product 27 forces the middle term 3). Sum = 3(r + 1/r + 1).
r + 1/r takes values in (−∞, −2] ∪ [2, ∞), so the sum takes values in (−∞, −3] ∪ [9, ∞), i.e. R − (−3, 9).
a = −3, b = 9, so a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> = 9 + 81 = 90.

qs.stem: For some θ ∈ (0, π/2), let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola x<sup>2</sup> − y<sup>2</sup> sec<sup>2</sup>θ = 8 be e<sub>1</sub> and l<sub>1</sub>, respectively, and let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse x<sup>2</sup> sec<sup>2</sup>θ + y<sup>2</sup> = 6 be e<sub>2</sub> and l<sub>2</sub>, respectively. If e<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = e<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>(sec<sup>2</sup>θ + 1), then (l<sub>1</sub>l<sub>2</sub>/(e<sub>1</sub>e<sub>2</sub>)) tan<sup>2</sup>θ is equal to ________.
steps: Hyperbola x<sup>2</sup>/8 − y<sup>2</sup>/(8cos<sup>2</sup>θ) = 1: e<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = 1 + cos<sup>2</sup>θ, l<sub>1</sub> = 2b<sup>2</sup>/a = 4√2 cos<sup>2</sup>θ. Ellipse x<sup>2</sup>/(6cos<sup>2</sup>θ) + y<sup>2</sup>/6 = 1 (major axis along y): e<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> = 1 − cos<sup>2</sup>θ, l<sub>2</sub> = 2√6 cos<sup>2</sup>θ.
Let c = cos<sup>2</sup>θ. The condition 1 + c = (1 − c)(1 + c)/c gives c = 1 − c, so c = 1/2 and tan<sup>2</sup>θ = 1.
e<sub>1</sub> = √(3/2), e<sub>2</sub> = √(1/2), l<sub>1</sub> = 2√2, l<sub>2</sub> = √6, so l<sub>1</sub>l<sub>2</sub>/(e<sub>1</sub>e<sub>2</sub>) = 4√3/(√3/2) = 8, and the required value is 8.

qs.stem: The value of ∑<sub>r=1</sub><sup>20</sup> | √( π ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>r</sup> x |sin πx| dx ) | is ________.
steps: Let I<sub>r</sub> = π ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>r</sup> x|sin πx| dx. Substituting x → r − x (|sin πx| has period 1 and is symmetric, so |sin π(r − x)| = |sin πx| for integer r) gives I<sub>r</sub> = (πr/2) ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>r</sup> |sin πx| dx.
∫<sub>0</sub><sup>r</sup> |sin πx| dx = r · (2/π), so I<sub>r</sub> = r<sup>2</sup> and the r-th term is r.

qs.stem: If k = tan( π/4 + (1/2)cos<sup>−1</sup>(2/3) ) + tan( (1/2)sin<sup>−1</sup>(2/3) ), then the number of solutions of the equation sin<sup>−1</sup>(kx − 1) = sin<sup>−1</sup>x − cos<sup>−1</sup>x is ________.
steps: Let θ = (1/2)cos<sup>−1</sup>(2/3), so cos 2θ = 2/3 and (1/2)sin<sup>−1</sup>(2/3) = π/4 − θ. Then k = tan(π/4 + θ) + tan(π/4 − θ) = 2/cos 2θ = 3.

Equation: sin<sup>−1</sup>(3x − 1) = 2 sin<sup>−1</sup>x − π/2. The domain needs |x| ≤ 1 and |3x − 1| ≤ 1, i.e. 0 ≤ x ≤ 2/3. Taking sine of both sides: 3x − 1 = −cos(2 sin<sup>−1</sup>x) = −(1 − 2x<sup>2</sup>) = 2x<sup>2</sup> − 1.
2x<sup>2</sup> − 3x = 0 gives x = 0 or 3/2; only x = 0 lies in the domain, and it checks (both sides equal −π/2). So 1 solution.

qs.stem: The electric current in the circuit is given as i = i0(t/T). The r.m.s current for the period t = 0 to t = T is ________.
steps: The mean of i2 over one period is (1)/(T) ∫0T i02t2/T2 dt.
Integrating gives i02/T3 × T3/3 = i02/3.
So irms = i0/√3.

qs.stem: Assuming in forward bias condition there is a voltage drop of 0.7 V across a silicon diode, the current through diode D<sub>1</sub> in the circuit is ________ mA. (Assume all diodes in the given circuit are identical)
steps: D<sub>2</sub> is connected the opposite way, so it is reverse biased and carries no current; D<sub>1</sub> and D<sub>3</sub> conduct and hold the node at 0.7 V.
Total current I = (12 − 0.7)/(0.3 × 10<sup>3</sup>) = 11.3/300 A ≈ 37.7 mA.
D<sub>1</sub> and D<sub>3</sub> are identical and in parallel, so each takes I/2 ≈ 18.8 mA.

qs.stem: For the two cells having same EMF E and internal resistance r, the current passing through the external resistor 6 Ω is same when both the cells are connected either in parallel or in series. The value of internal resistance r is ________ Ω.
steps: Series: I = 2E/(6 + 2r). Parallel: I = E/(6 + r/2).
Equating: 2(6 + r/2) = 6 + 2r, so 12 + r = 6 + 2r.
Hence r = 6 Ω.

qs.stem: Water drops fall from a tap on the floor, 5 m below, at regular intervals of time, the first drop strikes the floor when the sixth drop begins to fall. The height at which the fourth drop will be from ground, at the instant when the first drop strikes the ground is ________ m. (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Fall time of one drop: t = √(2h/g) = √(2 × 5/10) = 1 s.
Between the first and the sixth drop there are 5 equal intervals, so each interval is 0.2 s.
The fourth drop left 3 intervals (0.6 s) after the first, so it has fallen for 1 − 0.6 = 0.4 s: distance = ½(10)(0.4)<sup>2</sup> = 0.8 m.
Height above the ground = 5 − 0.8 = 4.2 m.

qs.stem: When both jaws of vernier callipers touch each other, zero mark of the vernier scale is right to zero mark of main scale, 4<sup>th</sup> mark on vernier scale coincides with certain mark on the main scale. While measuring the length of a cylinder, observer observes 15 divisions on main scale and 5th division of vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. Measured length of cylinder is ________ mm. (Least count of Vernier calliper = 0.1 mm)
steps: Zero error: the vernier zero lies to the right of the main zero and the 4th mark coincides, so the error is +4 × 0.1 = +0.4 mm.
Observed reading = 15 mm + 5 × 0.1 mm = 15.5 mm.
Corrected length = 15.5 − 0.4 = 15.1 mm.

qs.stem: Two wires A and B made of different matierals of lengths 6.0 cm and 5.4 cm, respectively and area of cross sections 3.0 × 10<sup>−5</sup> m<sup>2</sup> and 4.5 × 10<sup>−5</sup> m<sup>2</sup>, respectively are stretched by the same magnitude under a given load. The ratio of the Young's modulus of A to that of B is x : 3. The value of x is ________.
steps: Same load and same extension: Y = Fℓ/(AΔℓ), so Y ∝ ℓ/A.
Comparing with x : 3 gives x = 5.

qs.stem: A block of mass 5 kg is moving on an inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. Friction coefficient between the block and inclined plane surface is √3/2. The force to be applied on the block so that the block will move down without acceleration is ________ N. (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Component of weight down the plane: mg sin 30° = 5 × 10 × ½ = 25 N.
Kinetic friction (up the plane): μmg cos 30° = (√3/2)(50)(√3/2) = 37.5 N, larger than 25 N.
For zero acceleration the extra force must act down the plane: F + 25 = 37.5, so F = 12.5 N.

qs.stem: The magnitudes of power of a biconvex lens (refractive index 1.5) and that of a plano-concave lens (refractive index = 1.7) are same. If the curvature of planoconcave lens exactly matches with the curvature of back surface of the biconvex lens, then ratio of radius of curvature of front and back surface of the biconvex lens is ________.
steps: Let the biconvex lens have radii R<sub>1</sub> (front) and R<sub>2</sub> (back). Its power: 0.5(1/R<sub>1</sub> + 1/R<sub>2</sub>).
The plano-concave lens has curved radius R<sub>2</sub>: power magnitude 0.7/R<sub>2</sub>.
Equating: 0.5/R<sub>1</sub> + 0.5/R<sub>2</sub> = 0.7/R<sub>2</sub>, so 0.5/R<sub>1</sub> = 0.2/R<sub>2</sub>.
R<sub>1</sub>/R<sub>2</sub> = 5/2.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A plane wave after passing through prism remains as plane wave but passing through small pin hole may become spherical wave.
Statement II : The curvature of a spherical wave emerging from a slit will increase for increasing slit width.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Statement I: a prism only changes the direction of a plane wavefront, so it stays plane; a pin hole is a tiny aperture that diffracts the wave into a nearly spherical one. True.
Statement II: diffraction angle θ ≈ λ/a, so a wider slit spreads the wave less and the emerging front is flatter (less curved). The statement is false.
Hence I is true and II is false.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

qs.stem: In the following p-V diagram the equation of state along the curved path is given by (V − 2)<sup>2</sup> = 4ap where a is a constant. The total work done in the closed path is :
steps: At V = 1 and V = 3 the pressure is p<sub>0</sub> = (1)/(4a) (line AC); the curve A → B → C is a parabola with minimum p = 0 at V = 2, and the loop is completed along C → A.
Area enclosed = rectangle − area under parabola = 2p<sub>0</sub> − ∫<sub>1</sub><sup>3</sup>(V − 2)<sup>2</sup>/(4a) dV = 1/(2a) − 1/(6a) = 1/(3a).
Expansion occurs along the lower curve and compression along the higher line C → A, so the net work is negative: W = −1/(3a).

qs.stem: Two point charges of 1 nC and 2 nC are placed at the two corners of equilateral triangle of side 3 cm. The work done in bringing a charge of 3 nC from infinity to the third corner of the triangle is ______ μJ. (1/(4πε<sub>0</sub>) = 9 × 10<sup>9</sup> N.m<sup>2</sup>/C<sup>2</sup>)
steps: The potential at the third corner (each charge 3 cm away): V = k(q<sub>1</sub> + q<sub>2</sub>)/ℓ = 9 × 10<sup>9</sup> × 3 × 10<sup>−9</sup>/(3 × 10<sup>−2</sup>) = 900 V.
Work = q<sub>3</sub>V = 3 × 10<sup>−9</sup> × 900 = 2.7 × 10<sup>−6</sup> J = 2.7 μJ.

qs.stem: Two circular discs of radius each 10 cm are joined at their centres by a rod of length 30 cm and mass 600 gm as shown in figure. If the mass of each disc is 600 gm and applied torque between two discs is 43 × 10<sup>5</sup> dyne.cm, the angular acceleration of the discs about the given axis AB is ________ rad/s<sup>2</sup>.
steps: Axis AB is parallel to the plane of each disc: left disc centre is 10 cm from AB, right disc centre 20 cm from AB; the rod's midpoint is 5 cm from AB. Let m = 600 g, R = 10 cm.

Discs (about a diameter-parallel axis, then shifted): (¼mR<sup>2</sup> + mR<sup>2</sup>) + (¼mR<sup>2</sup> + 4mR<sup>2</sup>). Rod: m(3R)<sup>2</sup>/12 + m(R/2)<sup>2</sup> = 0.75mR<sup>2</sup> + 0.25mR<sup>2</sup> = mR<sup>2</sup>.
α = τ/I = 43 × 10<sup>5</sup>/(3.9 × 10<sup>5</sup>) ≈ 11 rad/s<sup>2</sup>.

qs.stem: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular loop of radius R is 16 μT. The magnetic field at a distance x = √3R on its axis from the centre is ______ μT.
steps: Centre: B<sub>0</sub> = μ<sub>0</sub>I/(2R) = 16 μT.
On the axis: B = μ<sub>0</sub>IR<sup>2</sup>/[2(R<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3/2</sup>]. With x<sup>2</sup> = 3R<sup>2</sup>, (R<sup>2</sup> + x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3/2</sup> = 8R<sup>3</sup>.
B = μ<sub>0</sub>I/(16R) = B<sub>0</sub>/8 = 2 μT.

qs.stem: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave travelling through a medium is given by E(x, t) = 25 sin(2.0 × 1015 t − 107 x)n then the refractive index of the medium is ________. (All given measurement are in SI units)
steps: Reading off the wave: ω = 2.0 × 10<sup>15</sup> rad/s, k = 10<sup>7</sup> m<sup>−1</sup>.
Wave speed v = ω/k = 2 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s.
n = c/v = (3 × 10<sup>8</sup>)/(2 × 10<sup>8</sup>) = 1.5.

qs.stem: Three long straight wires carrying current are arranged mutually parallel as shown in the figure. The force experienced by 15 cm length of wire Q is ________.
steps: P (3 A, up) and Q (1 A, down) carry opposite currents, so P repels Q, pushing it towards R: force per length = 2 × 10<sup>−7</sup> × 3 × 1/0.03 = 2 × 10<sup>−5</sup> N/m.
R (2 A, down) and Q (1 A, down) are parallel, so R attracts Q, again towards R: 2 × 10<sup>−7</sup> × 2 × 1/0.02 = 2 × 10<sup>−5</sup> N/m.
Net = 4 × 10<sup>−5</sup> N/m towards R; for 0.15 m, F = 6 × 10<sup>−6</sup> N towards R.

qs.stem: 10 kg of ice at −10 °C is added to 100 kg of water to lower its temperature from 25 °C. Consider no heat exchange to surroundings. The decrement to the temperature of water is ________ °C. (specific heat of ice = 2100 J/kg.°C, specific heat of water = 4200 J/kg.°C, latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.36 × 10<sup>5</sup> J/kg)
steps: Heat to bring ice to 0 °C: 10 × 2100 × 10 = 2.1 × 10<sup>5</sup> J; to melt it: 10 × 3.36 × 10<sup>5</sup> = 3.36 × 10<sup>6</sup> J.
Final temperature T: 2.1 × 10<sup>5</sup> + 3.36 × 10<sup>6</sup> + 10 × 4200 T = 100 × 4200 (25 − T).
3.57 × 10<sup>6</sup> + 42000T = 10.5 × 10<sup>6</sup> − 420000T, so T = 15 °C.
Fall in temperature of the water = 25 − 15 = 10 °C.

qs.stem: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with 4 Ω resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell is shunted with 12 Ω resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm. The internal resistance of cell is ________ Ω.
steps: With shunt S the terminal voltage is E S/(r + S), balanced against a potential gradient k per cm.
E·4/(r + 4) = 120k and E·12/(r + 12) = 180k.
r = 4 Ω.

qs.stem: A convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and focal length f = 18 cm is immersed in water. The difference in focal lengths of the given lens when it is in water and in air is a × f. The value of a is ________. (refractive index of water = 4/3)
steps: Lens-maker's formula: 1/f ∝ (n<sub>lens</sub>/n<sub>medium</sub> − 1). In air this is 0.5; in water it is 1.5/(4/3) − 1 = 0.125.
So f<sub>water</sub>/f<sub>air</sub> = 0.5/0.125 = 4, i.e. f<sub>water</sub> = 72 cm.
Difference = 72 − 18 = 54 cm = 3 × 18, so a = 3.

qs.stem: The displacement of a particle, executing simple harmonic motion with time period T, is expressed as x(t) = A sin ωt, where A is the amplitude. The maximum value of potential energy of this oscillator is found at t = T/2β. The value of β is ________.
steps: Potential energy (½kx<sup>2</sup>) is maximum at the extreme positions, x = ±A.
Starting from the mean position at t = 0 with x = A sin ωt, x first reaches A when ωt = π/2, i.e. t = T/4.
T/4 = T/(2β) gives β = 2.

qs.stem: The ratio of de Broglie wavelength of a deutron with kinetic energy E to that of an alpha particle with kinetic energy 2E, is n : 1. The value of n is ________. (Assume mass of proton = mass of neutron)
steps: λ = h/√(2mK), so λ<sub>d</sub>/λ<sub>α</sub> = √(m<sub>α</sub>K<sub>α</sub>/(m<sub>d</sub>K<sub>d</sub>)).
With m<sub>d</sub> = 2m, m<sub>α</sub> = 4m, K<sub>d</sub> = E, K<sub>α</sub> = 2E: ratio = √(4m × 2E/(2m × E)) = √4.
So n = 2.

qs.stem:
Regarding the hydrides of group 15 elements EH3 (E = N, P, As, Sb), select the correct statement from the following:
A. The stability of hydrides decreases down the group.
B. The basicity of hydrides decreases down the group.
C. The reducing character increases down the group.
D. The boiling point increases down the group.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Down the group E–H bonds lengthen and weaken: stability falls (NH<sub>3</sub> > PH<sub>3</sub> > AsH<sub>3</sub> > SbH<sub>3</sub>), so A is true and the reducing power rises, so C is true.
Lone pair is on a larger, more diffuse orbital down the group, so basicity falls: B is true.
Boiling point is not regular: NH<sub>3</sub> is abnormally high because of H-bonding, PH<sub>3</sub> is lowest, then AsH<sub>3</sub> < SbH<sub>3</sub>. So D is false. Correct: A, B, C.

qs.stem: An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. The time taken for decomposition to (1/8)<sup>th</sup> and (1/10)<sup>th</sup> of its initial concentration are t<sub>1/8</sub> and t<sub>1/10</sub> respectively. What is the value of (t<sub>1/8</sub>)/(t<sub>1/10</sub>) × 10 ? (log 2 = 0.3)
steps: First order: t = (2.303/k) log(C<sub>0</sub>/C). So t<sub>1/8</sub> = (2.303/k) log 8 and t<sub>1/10</sub> = (2.303/k) log 10.
Ratio = log 8 / log 10 = 3 × 0.3 / 1 = 0.9.
Multiplying by 10 gives 9.

qs.stem: Consider a weak base 'B' of pK<sub>b</sub> = 5.699. 'x' mL of 0.02 M HCl and 'y' mL of 0.02 M weak base 'B' are mixed to make 100 mL of a buffer of pH 9 at 25°C. The values of 'x' and 'y' respectively are: [Given: log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771, log 5 = 0.699]
steps: HCl converts part of B to BH<sup>+</sup>: salt = 0.02x, remaining base = 0.02(y − x) (in the same units).
pOH = 14 − 9 = 5 = 5.699 + log(x/(y − x)), so log(x/(y − x)) = −0.699, i.e. x/(y − x) = 1/5, giving y = 6x.
x + y = 100 gives 7x = 100, so x = 14.3 mL and y = 85.7 mL.

qs.stem: Consider the following reaction sequence: Compound (x) [76.6% C, 6.38% H, vapour density 47] → (i) CO<sub>2</sub>, NaOH, 120°C, high pressure; (ii) H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> → Compound (y) (Major Product). Compound (y) develops characteristic colour with neutral FeCl<sub>3</sub> solution. Identify the INCORRECT statement from the following for the above sequence.
steps: Molar mass = 2 × 47 = 94; C = 0.766 × 94 ≈ 72 (6 C), H ≈ 6, O = 94 − 78 = 16 (1 O): C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O, phenol (x). Kolbe reaction gives salicylic acid (y).
Both are acidic enough for NaOH, both are aromatic (sooty flame), and salicylic acid (carboxylic acid) liberates CO<sub>2</sub> from NaHCO<sub>3</sub>.
Salicylic acid is a stronger acid than phenol, so 'x is more acidic than y' is incorrect.
opts: Both compounds x and y will dissolve in NaOH.
Both compounds x and y will burn with sooty flame.
Compound y will dissolve in NaHCO<sub>3</sub> and evolve a gas.
Compound x is more acidic than compound y.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements for the following reaction sequence: Compound 'X' (molecular formula C3H6Cl2) → (excess of NaNH2) Compound 'Y'; Y → (dil. H2SO4, Hg2+) Compound 'Z'; Y → (red hot iron tube, Δ) Compound 'Q' (molecular formula C9H12).
Statement I: Compound 'Z' will give yellow precipitate with NaOI.
Statement II: Compound 'Q' has two different types of 'H' atoms (aromatic : aliphatic) in the ratio 1 : 3.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: X is a dichloropropane; double dehydrohalogenation with excess NaNH<sub>2</sub> gives propyne (Y). Hydration of propyne gives acetone (Z), a methyl ketone.
Acetone gives the iodoform test (yellow CHI<sub>3</sub>) with NaOI: Statement I is true.
Cyclic trimerisation of propyne gives 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (C<sub>9</sub>H<sub>12</sub>): 3 aromatic H and 9 methyl H, ratio 1 : 3. Statement II is true.
opts: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of species among BF4−, SiF4, XeF4 and SF4, that have unequal E–F bond lengths is two. Here, E is the central atom.
Statement II: Among O2−, O22−, F2 and O2+, O2− has the highest bond order.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: BF<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> (tetrahedral), SiF<sub>4</sub> (tetrahedral) and XeF<sub>4</sub> (square planar) have all E–F bonds equal; only SF<sub>4</sub> (see-saw) has axial and equatorial bonds of different length. So only one species, and Statement I is false.

Bond orders: O<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup> = 1.5, O<sub>2</sub><sup>2−</sup> = 1, F<sub>2</sub> = 1, O<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> = 2.5. The highest is O<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup>, not O<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>, so Statement II is false.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem: At T(K), 2 moles of liquid A and 3 moles of liquid B are mixed. The vapour pressure of ideal solution formed is 320 mm Hg. At this stage, one mole of A and one mole of B are added to the solution. The vapour pressure is now measured as 328.6 mm Hg. The vapour pressure (in mm Hg) of A and B respectively are:
steps: Raoult's law, first mixture: (2/5)P<sub>A</sub>° + (3/5)P<sub>B</sub>° = 320, so 2P<sub>A</sub>° + 3P<sub>B</sub>° = 1600.
After addition (3 mol A, 4 mol B): (3/7)P<sub>A</sub>° + (4/7)P<sub>B</sub>° = 328.6 ≈ 2300/7, so 3P<sub>A</sub>° + 4P<sub>B</sub>° = 2300.
Solving: P<sub>B</sub>° = 200 and P<sub>A</sub>° = 500 mm Hg.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of pairs, from the following, in which both the ions are coloured in aqueous solution is 3.
[Sc3+, Ti3+], [Mn2+, Cr2+], [Cu2+, Zn2+] and [Ni2+, Ti4+]
Statement II: Th4+ is the strongest reducing agent among Th4+, Ce4+, Gd3+ and Eu2+
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: Colourless (d<sup>0</sup> or d<sup>10</sup>): Sc<sup>3+</sup>, Zn<sup>2+</sup>, Ti<sup>4+</sup>. So only the pair [Mn<sup>2+</sup>, Cr<sup>2+</sup>] has both ions coloured: the count is 1, not 3. Statement I is false.
Th<sup>4+</sup> (f<sup>0</sup>) is very stable and has no tendency to be oxidised; Eu<sup>2+</sup> readily goes to Eu<sup>3+</sup> and is the good reducing agent. Statement II is false.
opts: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem:
Ph–CH=CH2 → (HBr, (PhCOO)2) Product. Consider the above reaction.
A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate.
B. The role of peroxide is to generate H• (Hydrogen radical).
C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a byproduct.
D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is formed as the minor product.
E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate.
Identify the correct statements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Peroxide homolysis gives PhCOO•, which loses CO<sub>2</sub> to give Ph•; Ph• abstracts H from HBr to give benzene and Br•. So the peroxide produces Br• (B false) and benzene is a by-product (C true).
Br• adds to the terminal carbon giving the more stable benzylic radical (A true); the product 1-bromo-2-phenylethane is the major product (D false).
Without peroxide, ordinary electrophilic (Markovnikov) addition goes via the benzylic carbocation (E true). Correct: A, C, E.

qs.stem: CORRECT order of stability for the following is: CH<sub>2</sub>=CH<sup>−</sup>, CH<sub>3</sub>–CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>, CH≡C<sup>−</sup>
steps: Carbanion stability rises with s-character of the carbon holding the lone pair (the electrons sit closer to the nucleus).
Acetylide is sp (50% s), vinyl anion is sp<sup>2</sup> (33% s), ethyl anion is sp<sup>3</sup> (25% s).
Order: HC≡C<sup>−</sup> > CH<sub>2</sub>=CH<sup>−</sup> > CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>.

qs.stem: In period 4 of the periodic table, the elements with highest and lowest atomic radii are respectively.
steps: Radius decreases from left to right across a period as nuclear charge rises with the same shell.
In period 4 the leftmost element is K (largest) and, among the options, the far-right halogen Br has the smallest radius.
Na, Cl are period 3 and Rb is period 5, so the answer is K & Br.

qs.stem: 20.0 dm<sup>3</sup> of an ideal gas 'X' at 600 K and 0.5 MPa undergoes isothermal reversible expansion until pressure of the gas is 0.2 MPa. Which of the following option is correct? (Given: log 2 = 0.3010 and log 5 = 0.6989)
steps: Isothermal ideal gas: ΔU = ΔH = 0, so q = −w.
w = −2.303 P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> log(P<sub>1</sub>/P<sub>2</sub>) with P<sub>1</sub>V<sub>1</sub> = 0.5×10<sup>6</sup> Pa × 0.020 m<sup>3</sup> = 10<sup>4</sup> J.
log(2.5) = 0.6989 − 0.3010 = 0.3979, so w = −2.303 × 10<sup>4</sup> × 0.3979 ≈ −9.1 kJ and q = +9.1 kJ.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Griss-Ilosvay test is used for the detection of nitrite ion, which involves the use of sulphanilic acid and α-naphthylamine reagent.
Statement II: In the above test, sulphanilic acid is diazotized by the acidified nitrite ion, which on further coupling with α-naphthylamine forms an azo-dye.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: The Griess-Ilosvay test detects nitrite using sulphanilic acid and α-naphthylamine: Statement I is true.
In acid, nitrite gives HNO<sub>2</sub>, which diazotises the aromatic amine of sulphanilic acid; the diazonium salt then couples with α-naphthylamine to give a red azo dye. Statement II is true.
opts: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

qs.stem: The correct statement among the following is:
steps: Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub>: Ni(0), strong-field CO pairs the 4s electrons into 3d<sup>10</sup>, sp<sup>3</sup>, no unpaired electrons: diamagnetic.
[Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: Ni<sup>2+</sup> d<sup>8</sup> with strong-field CN<sup>−</sup> pairs up, dsp<sup>2</sup> square planar: diamagnetic.
[NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup>: weak-field Cl<sup>−</sup>, d<sup>8</sup> unpaired (2 electrons), sp<sup>3</sup> tetrahedral: paramagnetic.
opts: Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub> is diamagnetic and [NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> and [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> are paramagnetic.
Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub> and [NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> are diamagnetic and [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> is paramagnetic.
Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub> and [Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> are diamagnetic and [NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> is paramagnetic.
[Ni(CN)<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> and [NiCl<sub>4</sub>]<sup>2−</sup> are diamagnetic and Ni(CO)<sub>4</sub> is paramagnetic.

qs.stem: The wave numbers of three spectral lines of H atom are considered. Identify the set of spectral lines belonging to Balmer series. (R = Rydberg constant)
steps: Balmer lines end at n = 2: 1/λ = R(1/4 − 1/n<sup>2</sup>).
This matches the first set.

qs.stem: 0.53 g of an organic compound (x) when heated with excess of nitric acid (concentrated) and then with silver nitrate gave 0.75 g of silver bromide precipitate. 1.0 g of (x) gave 1.32 g of CO<sub>2</sub> gas on combustion. The percentage of hydrogen in the compound (x) is ____%. [Nearest Integer] [Given: Molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup> H: 1, C: 12, Br: 80, Ag: 108, O: 16; Compound (x): C<sub>x</sub>H<sub>y</sub>Br<sub>z</sub>]
steps: The compound contains only C, H, Br, so %H = 100 − 60.2 − 36 = 3.8 ≈ 4.

qs.stem: Consider the dissociation equilibrium of the following weak acid HA ⇌ H<sup>+</sup>(aq) + A<sup>−</sup>(aq). If the pK<sub>a</sub> of the acid is 4, then the pH of 10 mM HA solution is ______. (Nearest integer) [Given: The degree of dissociation can be neglected with respect to unity]
steps: K<sub>a</sub> = 10<sup>−4</sup>, C = 10 mM = 10<sup>−2</sup> M.
With α << 1: [H<sup>+</sup>] = √(K<sub>a</sub>C) = √(10<sup>−6</sup>) = 10<sup>−3</sup> M.
pH = 3.

qs.stem: X is the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by [Pt(NH<sub>3</sub>)(H<sub>2</sub>O)BrCl]. Y is the number of optically inactive isomer(s) exhibited by [CrCl<sub>2</sub>(ox)<sub>2</sub>]<sup>3−</sup>. Z is the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>(NO<sub>2</sub>)<sub>3</sub>]. The value of X + Y + Z is _____.
steps: Square planar [Pt(a)(b)(c)(d)] (Mabcd) has 3 geometrical isomers: X = 3.
[CrCl<sub>2</sub>(ox)<sub>2</sub>]<sup>3−</sup> (M(AA)<sub>2</sub>b<sub>2</sub>): the trans form has a mirror plane (optically inactive); the cis form is chiral (a pair of enantiomers). Y = 1.
[Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>3</sub>(NO<sub>2</sub>)<sub>3</sub>] (Ma<sub>3</sub>b<sub>3</sub>): fac and mer, Z = 2. Total = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6.

qs.stem: Consider the following redox reaction taking place in acidic medium BH<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup>(aq) + ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>(aq) → H<sub>2</sub>BO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>(aq) + Cl<sup>−</sup>(aq). If the Nernst equation for the above balanced reaction is E<sub>cell</sub> = E°<sub>cell</sub> − (RT/nF) ln Q, then the value of n is ________. (Nearest integer)
steps: BH<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> → H<sub>2</sub>BO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>: the four hydridic H (−1) become +1, losing 8 e<sup>−</sup> per BH<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup>. ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> → Cl<sup>−</sup>: gains 6 e<sup>−</sup>.
Balance electrons: 3 BH<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> (24 e<sup>−</sup>) with 4 ClO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> (24 e<sup>−</sup>).
So n = 24.

qs.stem: 500 mL of 1.2 M KI solution is mixed with 500 mL of 0.2 M KMnO<sub>4</sub> solution in basic medium. The liberated iodine was titrated with standard 0.1 M Na<sub>2</sub>S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> solution in the presence of starch indicator till the blue color disappeared. The volume (in L) of Na<sub>2</sub>S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> consumed is _____. (Nearest integer)
steps: In basic medium MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> → MnO<sub>2</sub> takes 3 e<sup>−</sup>: 0.5 L × 0.2 M × 3 = 0.3 equivalents; KI (0.6 mol, 1 e<sup>−</sup> each) is in excess, so KMnO<sub>4</sub> is limiting.
I<sub>2</sub> formed corresponds to 0.3 equivalents (0.15 mol I<sub>2</sub>).
I<sub>2</sub> + 2S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup> → 2I<sup>−</sup> + S<sub>4</sub>O<sub>6</sub><sup>2−</sup>: thiosulfate needed = 0.3 mol; V = 0.3 / 0.1 = 3 L.
